title: Real-time presence
description: Who is online, viewing or typing in a room for multi-tenant server apps: join, heartbeat and leave per tab, members grouped by user, TTL expiry and sweep, small validated JSON state (cursors, typing), ordered join/update/leave events with throttled updates, and a Server-Sent Events Fetch adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build, TextEncoder/TextDecoder, structuredClone, ReadableStream and the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
The SSE stream needs a runtime that keeps a response open; short serverless timeouts end it and EventSource reconnects with a fresh snapshot.
Framework-neutral core; mount the HTTP adapter with your framework's catch-all route.
No runtime packages, environment reads or network activity at install or import time; timers start only for open streams and pending throttled updates.

configuration: For one server instance use MemoryPresenceStore; for several, implement PresenceStore on Redis (a sorted set per room scored by expiry, see CONTRACT.md) and forward events between instances through your own pub/sub.
Implement authorize(actor, action, {tenantId, room}) for join (also heartbeat) and read (list, stream) from your own membership and document-access checks.
Implement authenticate(request) from your session or verified token, never from the request body or query string.
Call presence.sweep() on an interval (for example every ttlMs / 2) so expired tabs emit leave even when nobody lists the room.
Tune ttlMs (30 s), maxPerRoom (500), maxStateBytes (1024) and minUpdateMs (100 ms); keep the client heartbeat or stream ping below ttlMs.
Mount createPresenceHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins; it complements, not replaces, your CSRF policy.
limitations: Event fan-out and seq numbering are in-process; several instances need a shared store and your own pub/sub, and seq restarts when a room becomes empty and unwatched (clients resync from the snapshot).
No Redis client or WebSocket server is included; the Redis shape is documented only, and the transport is Server-Sent Events plus POST.

Join/leave decisions are serialized per room within one process; across instances, simultaneous last-tab changes can emit a duplicate or missing join/leave unless the store and pub/sub serialize them.
Presence is ephemeral and not an audit log; it does not persist history or prove that a person read anything.
No rate limiting; add request rate limits (see the rate-limit module) on heartbeat and stream routes.
Session security, production load behavior and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: transport is SSE GET {prefix}/stream plus POST {prefix}/heartbeat and /leave; no WebSocket
full room → 409 room-full; oversized state → 413 state-too-large; throttled updates keep the latest state
options: ttlMs: expiry after last heartbeat (default 30 s), maxPerRoom (default 500)
maxStateBytes (default 1,024), minUpdateMs: per-user update throttle (default 100 ms)

behaviors: several tabs of one user list once with a connection count, the newest state and the earliest joinedAt
a user's first connection emits join and the last leave emits leave; extra tabs emit only update
re-joining an own connection refreshes it instead of adding a second one; leave is idempotent
expired connections are hidden by list and removed by sweep, which returns leave events per room
state must be plain JSON (finite numbers, no Date, Map, functions or undefined, bounded depth) within maxStateBytes in UTF-8 bytes
seq is strictly increasing per room and independent across rooms; the snapshot carries the current seq
update events are coalesced per user to one per minUpdateMs on a fake clock, emitting the latest state, and dropped when the user leaves
the same room name in another tenant is another room; outsiders and read-only users cannot join, read-only users can list
only the actor who joined a connection may heartbeat, leave or re-join it
maxPerRoom counts connections and refuses with room-full until expiry frees space
SSE stream: snapshot first, then join/update/leave events with id equal to seq, ping comments, and leave when the request's AbortSignal fires
SSE stream refuses signed-out (401), unauthorized or foreign-origin (403), invalid (400) and full-room (409) requests without leaving a connection behind
HTTP heartbeat and leave: 200, 401, 403 origin and ownership, 404, 405, 413 for large state or body, 400 for bad JSON, cache-control no-store

changes: First release: core, in-memory store and Server-Sent Events Fetch adapter.
